fix(rules): the catalogue sees the per-surface rules (S13)

`rules list` reported 12 rules and the package ships 16. The four missing ones are
`rules/mdc/*.mdc`, and the reason they were invisible is structural rather than an
oversight: `loadRules` reads `rules/*.md` and `rules/stacks/*.md`, which is every
rule that is a *stack profile*. The per-surface rules are projected by `ruleBodies`
inside `desiredRegion` instead, so they were in every repository's AGENTS.md and
invisible to all three catalogue commands.

The reader-visible part: an agent told to run `simt rules why test-gate` — by a
line in its own AGENTS.md — got "no rule with that id". `rules why` is the command
whose entire purpose is answering "why is this rule here", and it could not answer
about four of them.

The fix is in the catalogue, not in `loadRules`, and the reason is worth recording
because the obvious place is the wrong one. `loadRules`'s result is `select`ed and
`render`ed into the region; the per-surface bodies are added separately. Putting
them in `loadRules` would project every one of them twice — once as a profile
section, once as `## Process:` — which is the duplication ADR-046 exists to prevent.
Verified rather than reasoned: the mutation that moves them into `loadRules` is
caught.

Also, the `applies` column. An opt-in rule has an EMPTY `simt-applies` array, and
`-` is a true reading of that which answers none of the questions a reader has;
`simt-opt-in` is why the array is empty, and that is the fact worth printing. It only
became visible once these rules entered the catalogue, and `-` was the answer for
one of them until now.

Two tests, four mutations. Reverting the union fails; moving the rules into
`loadRules` fails; a duplicated `## Process:` heading fails the guard that exists for
it; and an existing expectation that was written while these rules were invisible now
says why it was wrong about the answer rather than about the loader. 772/772.
